title: Pollen, finished basements, and why Fairfax County ducts load faster than they look
headline: Pollen, finished basements, and why Fairfax County ducts load faster than they look
description: McLean, VA sits under mature oaks with finished basements and humid summers. why returns fill with pollen, how basement trunks sweat, and when to clean the ducts.

sections.heading: The backyard is beautiful. The returns are full of it.
paragraphs: McLean’s lot sizes and tree cover are the reason people move there. Oak, maple, and pine dump pollen onto decks, cars, and outdoor furniture every spring. The HVAC does not stay outside. Return grilles pull that load into the trunk lines, especially in houses where a finished basement shares air with the main floors.
Add Fairfax County summer humidity — still fed by the Potomac even when you cannot see the river from Langley — and cold metal ducts in a basement start to sweat.

sections.heading: Finished basements are a moisture shortcut
paragraphs: Many McLean colonials put the air handler in a basement along Difficult Run, Pimmit Run, or a low lot. The room feels cool. The ducts are cooler still. Humid air condenses on the outside and inside of those trunks. Dust and pollen stick. The blower then sends that mix upstairs.
Tysons condos next door fail a different way: long dryer vents and tight closets. Lint and moisture have nowhere to go if the cap is packed.
If dust returns days after you wipe the registers, when you are ready to book, use the [McLean, VA location page](/locations/mclean).

sections.heading: What McLean households usually notice
paragraphs: A large house can hide a dirty system for years because the square footage dilutes the smell. Watch for:
listItems: A musty note from basement supplies when the AC starts after a wet week.
Yellow-gray film on registers during peak pollen season.
Allergy flare-ups that are worse at home than at the office.

paragraphs: McLean jobs are scheduled from our metro offices For service and scheduling, see the [local service page](/locations/mclean).
You do not need to clear the lot. You need a dry, clear air path. McLean is served from our [Burke](/locations/burke) office — the same dispatch as [Arlington](/locations/arlington).
The [McLean location page](/locations/mclean) has neighborhoods, packages, and booking. Pair ducts with [dryer vent cleaning](/dryer-vent-cleaning) if a second-floor laundry has a long run.
listItems: Run a dehumidifier in finished basements and keep indoor humidity under 50%.
Change filters during heavy pollen weeks, not just on a 90-day calendar.
Clean ducts every 3 to 5 years; clear dryer vents about once a year.

faq.q: Does construction near McLean change cleaning intervals?
faq.a: Active drywall work nearby often shortens the useful interval. Wait until heavy dust settles, then inspect.

faq.q: Should I clean ducts after renovations?
faq.a: Yes if sanding or drywall dust entered returns. Otherwise a standard 3–5 year interval is typical.

faq.q: What proof should a cleaning include?
faq.a: Before-and-after photos of trunks or vents, plus a clear scope agreed before work starts.
